questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Brisbane because it was further north, meaning i would have great weather the entire stay and i would be closer to The Great Barrier Reef where i would be able to scuba dive.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a really great exchange semester!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty okay

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive much information but i also didn't seek it out. I didn't feel like i needed assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation was fine but you didn't really get a lot out of it except that a third of the exchange students were from Norway and to be careful around magpies (a bird)

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Where i lived it was pretty easy to find accommodation. It was however very overpriced. I lived in Student One on Adelaide street. 
If i could do it differently i would have booked a hostel the first month and find a sharehouse through an app called "Flatmates". If you're lucky you can find rooms that are somewhere between 3000-4000 dkk pr month.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Busses in CBD are pretty well connected but if you find accommodation further from the center be mindful of the public transport because the suburbs can be pretty far from decent public transport.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process was overall pretty chill

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You sign up to the different units you're going to take couple months in advance. They don't post the actual timetables until schedule selections but you can usually get an idea of when the classes are from previous years. You then have a couple weeks to send in a prioritized request for the different timeslots and a week after it closes you get your final timetable.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could call or write to HiQ. They were generally pretty good at helping

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all wanted that i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The process is pretty relaxed so don't stress to much about it

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level at the science faculty was pretty low compared to KU. I had a 600 course and it compared to 1./2. year on molecular biomedicine and a 400 course that compared to 3. g in high school.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had to hand in things throughout the semester that counted a percentage towards my final grade. Also, there is a lot more handholding in the lab than what you'd get at KU. You could barely do anything in lab without an assistant that would come and help you.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MXB107 Introduction to Statistical Modelling
LQB485 Cell Biology
LQB682 Biomolecular Design
KNB127 CGI Foundations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: KNB127 CGI Foundations was a really fun and very different course. I got to learn how to make a 3D model in a program called Maya

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Visa and OSHC (around 5000 dkk in total)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were generally a bit more expensive than in DK but barista coffee was a lot cheaper (20 dkk)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They had a lot of different clubs but many of them seemed geared towards other cultures or elite sorts. If you're into climbing the climbing club is very active and very social. 
I ended up joining a club at UQ because they had a dive club (UniDive). If you have a scuba license i would definitely recommend this one since it made diving near Brisbane a lot cheaper than you you did it through a company.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on a surf trip with QUT surfers. Its pretty much just other exchange students so you have a great opportunity to socialize

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Find a group of friends (4-7) and rent your own 4WD at Fraser (K'gari). 
Go to North Stradbroke island, they have free roaming kangaroos and koalas.
Go to New Zealand, rent a car/auto camper and go on amazing hikes.
Go on a boat trip at Whitsundays
Stop by Tin Can Bay to feed dolphins.
If you have i divers license, go to Wolf Rock and dive with 30+ nurse sharks. Also, fly to Fiji to dive with bull sharks!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The only issue i found was that you do everything on the left instead of the right (roads, escalators, passing other people on the street)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to all the intro events. This is when the friend groups are formed

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Remembering that they have a lot of dangerous animals

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness towards strangers

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) I you have time, fly to Brisbane at least a week before the semester starts so you have time to acclimate. I didn't and had a very stressful start
2) Go to sports events and se rugby/AFL/cricket. It's really fun
3) Travel around the area. Brisbane is within 2 hours of a lot of really amazing things.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Relax and enjoy your time. Its pretty easy passing the courses so make sure you spend time enjoying Australia and everything it has to offer

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The travels! I had so many crazy adventures traveling Australia and surrounding countries like New Zealand and Fiji

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not celebrating Christmas with my family

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
